items.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: when I moved to New York I became friends with the same sort of a musical association that he had, I’m talking about social. And so I knew him largely as just a person that you sit and chat with you know.

ctx.x: Did you have opportunities to hear the Basie band a number of times?

Yes. Whenever I possibly could. And of course thank God for television, because we got to see quite a bit of that in the latter years. But he had such a wonderful, he and Duke Ellington both achieved a wonderful concept of an orchestral sound and a style. Now this is an incredible thing to do, because you know there are literally thousands of jazz bands and how many of them are distinctive? And he was distinctive. Now to get back to Joe Williams of course, I had heard Joe sing, you know for years and years I’d…
think he’s also an amazing singer. And he took the blues out of the sin and gin era, and you know the dark, dank music halls or clubs or anything—
